title: Wegener to Modern Tectonics
welcome_lead: Trace theory from 1912 continental drift to modern plates.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on Wegener, sea floor spreading and tectonic theory development.
final_note: Wegener proposed it; mid-ocean ridges proved it.

concepts.def: Wegener's 1912 hypothesis: continents move slowly; based on fit, fossils, climate.
Supercontinent ~250 Ma ago, broke up to form modern continents.
Hess (1962): new crust forms at mid-ocean ridges; oceans widen.
Magnetic stripes in ocean floor record reversals, confirming spreading.
Alfred Wegener (1880-1930), German meteorologist who first proposed continental drift.
Synthesis from 1960s: 7 major + many minor plates moving on asthenosphere.

walkthroughs.body_html: Coastline fit (S. America-Africa), Glossopteris fossil distribution across southern continents, glacial striations on tropical Africa, Permian coal in Antarctica. Lacking a mechanism, his theory rejected by geologists until 1960s.

Harry Hess (1962) proposed mid-ocean ridges produce new basaltic crust as mantle convects upward. Atlantic widens about 2.5 cm/yr. Vine-Matthews-Morley (1963) found symmetric magnetic stripes confirming hypothesis using paleomagnetism.

Seven major plates: Pacific, North American, Eurasian, African, Antarctic, Indo-Australian, South American. GPS measures plate velocities: Pacific moves NW at ~7 cm/yr relative to Eurasia. San Andreas Fault accommodates this transform motion in California.
